post.caption: This 2,000-year-old crown folds for travel. In 1978, a Soviet-Afghan team led by Viktor Sarianidi found it. It came from six graves, for five women and one man, and they held more than 20,000 items of gold and precious metal. The treasures were later hidden in Kabul's presidential palace vault, and only a handful of trusted people knew. In 2004, the keys to the gold safe could not be found, so a locksmith opened it with a circular saw. About 30 people watched, including the archaeologist who found it. It then toured museums from Paris to New York.
